sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: In a real debate you must frame the question, test the premise and rebut without losing composure.

blocks.text: Framing sets the terms of the debate. A precise question (“Sollte die Stadt den Autoverkehr in der Innenstadt begrenzen?”) is easier to argue than a vague one (“Ist Verkehr gut?”). Name the premise behind each position so the disagreement becomes visible.

A rebuttal targets the argument, not the person. Acknowledge the strongest version of the opposing view, identify the premise you reject, and offer evidence or a counterexample. Keep your tone calm; in German debate, composure is read as competence.

blocks.title: Attack the premise, not the speaker
blocks.text: “Diese Argumentation setzt voraus, dass …” is a powerful move: it shows what would have to be true for the other side to work.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Die entscheidende Frage ist, ob die Maßnahme wirkt.
Diese Argumentation setzt voraus, dass die Daten vollständig sind.
Dieser Einwand lässt sich widerlegen, weil die Daten fehlen.
Die Gegenposition betont hingegen die langfristigen Kosten.

items: “Voraussetzen” means to presuppose: Das setzt voraus, dass …
“Widerlegen” is stronger than “bezweifeln”; use it only when you can show the argument fails.
“Hingegen” signals a contrast and often follows the verb.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

blocks.text: German debate can sound blunt to outsiders, but the norm is argument-based criticism rather than personal attack. Naming a flaw in an argument is expected, not rude.
In formal settings, speakers often begin with a concession (“Zwar …”) before moving to their objection. This signals that they have listened and strengthens the rebuttal.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Framing, challenging, rebutting
sections.lede: Each move has a fixed structure that keeps the exchange structured.

rows: Dieser Einwand lässt sich widerlegen, weil …

blocks.text: “Ob” introduces an indirect yes/no question, so the verb goes to the end: Die Frage ist, ob die Maßnahme wirkt.

sections.tip: Before you rebut, restate the opposing argument in its strongest form. A weak caricature is easy to dismiss and easy to spot.

exercises.prompt: Die entscheidende Frage ist, ___ die Maßnahme wirkt.

exercises.prompt: Build: “This objection can be refuted because the data are missing.”

exercises.explanation: Sich lassen plus infinitive expresses possibility; the weil-clause ends with fehlen.

exercises.explanation: Hingegen signals the contrast and follows the verb.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Frame a debate question, challenge one premise and rebut one objection.

model.de: Die entscheidende Frage ist, ob die Stadt den Autoverkehr begrenzen sollte. Diese Argumentation setzt voraus, dass alle Pendler Alternativen haben. Dieser Einwand lässt sich widerlegen, weil es bereits ein dichtes Busnetz gibt.
model.en: The decisive question is whether the city should limit car traffic. This argument presupposes that all commuters have alternatives. This objection can be refuted because there is already a dense bus network.

tips: Frame the question before you argue.
Challenge the premise, not the person.
Give a concrete reason or example in the rebuttal.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.wrong: Die Frage ist, ob wirkt die Maßnahme.
items.right: Die Frage ist, ob die Maßnahme wirkt.
items.why: The ob-clause puts the verb at the end.

items.wrong: Diese Argumentation setzt voraus, dass die Daten sind vollständig.
items.right: Diese Argumentation setzt voraus, dass die Daten vollständig sind.
items.why: The dass-clause ends with the verb sind.

items.wrong: Dieser Einwand lässt sich widerlegen, weil die Daten fehlen fehlen.
items.right: Dieser Einwand lässt sich widerlegen, weil die Daten fehlen.
items.why: The verb appears once, at the end of the weil-clause.
